newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli pig poster suspect goes to mental hospital.
newsitem.headline: Israeli pig poster suspect goes to mental hospital.

text.p: The Israeli woman accused of pasting posters on Hebron storefronts depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig was sent to hospital on Monday for psychiatric evaluation.
"She's on her way now," said her lawyer Shmuel Caspar. "It is one stepping stone on the way to freedom."
Prosecutors had wanted 26-year-old Tatyana Suskin to stay in jail for her mental evaluation. Defence lawyers requested she undergo the tests in a hospital near Tel Aviv.
The posters, pasted on June 27 across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of Hebron in the West Bank provoked an outpouring of Moslem rage and violent anti-Israeli protests.
Suskin will stay in the psychiatric ward "until a change of circumstances or until the end of the legal process," said High Court spokesman Moshe Gorali.
Suskin is accused of committing a racist act, harming religious sensitivities, supporting a terrorist group and endangering life by stoning an Arab car. The offences carry a maximum 26-year sentence.
At her first court appearance, Suskin wore a yellow shirt with the black clenched fist of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane.
